pins.title: Red Light Therapy at Home: Handheld vs Mid-Size Panel vs Full-Body (Which to Start With)
pins.subtitle: Match the device to your routine
pins.description: Home red light devices come in three sizes: handheld units for spot areas like a knee or elbow, mid-size panels that cover a back or torso in one session, and full-body panels for daily whole-body routines. Most people do best starting smaller than they think. See who each type fits. #redlighttherapy #homewellness #recoverytools #redlightpanel #selfcare #wellnessroutine

pins.title: Before You Buy a Red Light Therapy Panel: 5 Specs to Check (Wavelength, Irradiance and More)
pins.subtitle: What actually matters on the listing
pins.description: Comparing red light therapy panels? Check five things: stated wavelengths (for example 660nm and 850nm, not just 'red light'), irradiance in mW/cm2, EMF shielding, published third-party test results, and warranty length. A spec checklist to keep open while you shop. #redlighttherapy #redlightpanel #buyersguide #homewellness #recoverytools #biohacking

pins.title: The Biggest Red Light Therapy Mistake: Buying a Full-Body Panel You Won't Use
pins.subtitle: Start smaller than you think
pins.description: The most common way people go wrong with red light therapy isn't picking the wrong brand. It's buying a large full-body panel, using it for two weeks, and letting it collect dust. If you're new, a handheld or mid-size unit is the lower-risk way to find out whether you'll keep a routine. Research on benefits varies by use; not medical advice. #redlighttherapy #homewellness #recoverytools #wellnessroutine #smartshopping #selfcare
